title: A finite etale generic point on a finite normal cover
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$, with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=k(S)$. Let $P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a nonempty finite etale scheme. There exist a finite separable field extension $L/K$ and a $K$-morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to P$ with the following properties. The normalization $q:S_L\to S$ of $S$ in $L$ is a normal integral scheme, is finite, proper and surjective, and $S_L$ is of finite type over $k$. Its function field is identified with $L$ as a $K$-extension via the map induced by $q$. The canonical morphism $j_L:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S_L$ identifies its source with the generic point of $S_L$, and induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\simeq S_L\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Normalization is the affine integral-closure construction [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Separated means that the relative diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The other notions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-sc-generic-point] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its fibre is canonically $P$. Nonemptiness supplies a point $z\in P$; the cited statement gives a finite separable extension $L=\kappa(z)$ of $K$ and an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\simeq\{z\}$ over $K$. Compose with the open inclusion into $P$ to obtain $u$. This chooses one factor; no rational point over $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: The one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its only local ring is $k$, whose only ideals are $0$ and $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian, hence locally Noetherian and therefore quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] with $X=S$, $x=\eta$, $\kappa(\eta)=K$ and the finite extension $L/K$. Take its explicitly allowed normalization of $S$ in $h:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iii), over every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is the spectrum of the integral closure of $A$ in $\Gamma(h^{-1}U,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}L})$; this ring is $L$ for $U$ nonempty, because $U$ then contains $\eta$ and $h^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}L$, and it is $0$ for $U$ empty. Hence this normalization is exactly $q:S_L\to S$ of [def-fin-normalization-extension], and its natural factorization map is $j_L$. It supplies normality, integrality of $S_L$, and the canonical factorization $\operatorname{Spec}L\xrightarrow{j_L}S_L\xrightarrow{q}S$ through $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$. It also identifies $j_L$ with the generic point and its residue-field map with an isomorphism $k(S_L)\simeq L$. The factorization makes this an identification over $K$, since both induced maps $K\to L$ are the original extension map.

proof.text: By [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite], $q$ is finite: the base is integral of finite type over a field and $L/K$ is finite. Thus $q$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. This image contains $\eta$, because $qj_L$ is the generic-point map preceded by $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. A closed subset containing the generic point is all of $S$, proving surjectivity. Properness includes finite type, so composing $q$ with the finite-type structure map of $S$ gives finite type of $S_L/k$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change].

source.place: Tags 035B, lemma-ubiquity-nagata (1), and 0AVK, lemma-nagata-normalization-finite-general, specialize to the cited finite-normalization theorem; lemma-finite-proper; Tag 01T3, lemma-composition-finite-type

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $\eta\in U$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Write $B\subset L$ for the integral closure of $A$; the normalization definition identifies $q^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iii), applied to $h$ with $h^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}L$, identifies $j_L$ on this chart with $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow L$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies the whole generic fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A K)$, since $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ factors through $U$. Put $T=A\setminus\{0\}$. The map $B\otimes_A K\to T^{-1}B$, $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto ab/s$, is an isomorphism with inverse $b/s\mapsto b\otimes(1/s)$: the fraction relations and the tensor balancing relation give the two inverse identities. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $T^{-1}B$ is the integral closure of $K$ in $T^{-1}L=L$. Every element of $L$ is integral over $K$, since $L/K$ is finite. Hence $T^{-1}B=L$. The resulting isomorphism $B\otimes_A K\simeq L$ is $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$; on spectra its first component is precisely $j_L$ and its second is the prescribed $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. It therefore proves the claimed canonical isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}K$, not merely an abstract isomorphism of schemes.
